title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: hyperlinks in Edge warn and block notifications (Worldwide)
notes: claim 44: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
the verifier wrote "hold" but listed no blocker and fewer than three majors; the claims decide, so the page is not held
summary: Hold: the impact rationale promises that links appear only after an administrator supplies them, although Microsoft has not stated the arrival behaviour. The roadmap facts and control routes are supported, but the licensing paragraph also needs to acknowledge differing Microsoft guidance.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what happens to existing notifications when this hyperlink feature arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP hyperlink default Edge; notification changes existing rules rollout. Read roadmap 558688, DLP policy reference, Edge DLP page and endpoint settings. None states the arrival behaviour of this hyperlink option.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the presentation of this hyperlink in Edge's own notifications.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP Edge notification hyperlink Get Support; Endpoint DLP Edge notification hyperlink macOS display toast. Opened DLP policy reference and Edge DLP page; Windows Get Support is described, not Edge-specific rendering.

claims.claim: The printed Purview portal route reaches the service-domain and browser Block with override control in an existing DLP rule.
claims.quote: Data loss prevention > Policies ... Edit policy ... Customize advanced DLP rules ... edit ... Actions > Audit or restrict activities on Windows device ... Service domain and browser activities ... Block with override

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -EndpointDlpRestrictions @(@{"Setting"="<Setting>"; "Value"="Warn"}) is a documented operation for configuring Endpoint DLP restrictions.
claims.quote: Set-DlpComplianceRule [-Identity] <ComplianceRuleIdParameter> ... The EndpointDlpRestrictions parameter specifies the restricted endpoints for Endpoint DLP. ... The available values for <Value> are: Audit, Block, Ignore, or Warn.

claims.claim: Block and Warn EndpointDlpRestrictions values also require NotifyUser.
claims.quote: When you use the values Block or Warn in this parameter, also need to use the NotifyUser parameter.

claims.claim: EndpointDlpRestrictions requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator membership in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: This parameter requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Data loss prevention > Policies > policy > Edit policy > Customize advanced DLP rules > rule reaches the rule containing the notification customisation options.
claims.quote: ## Rules ... ### User notifications and policy tips ... If you selected Devices only ... plus the option to customize the notification title, content, and add a hyperlink in the form of a Get Support button
claims.fix: Keep the printed route, whose navigation is confirmed by the already-cited unauthorized-data-sharing guide. Replace the note with: 'Route ends at the rule. In its user notifications and policy tips, policies scoped to Devices only offer a custom notification title, content and a Get Support hyperlink; the policy reference gives no further UI step labels.'

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no automation operation for setting the device notification Get Support hyperlink.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP hyperlink PowerShell; Set-DlpComplianceRule NotifyPolicyTipCustomDialog. Opened and searched Set-DlpComplianceRule for hyperlink, Get Support, toast and notification; URL is Exchange-only, custom dialog has no device mapping.

claims.claim: The deployment guide lists Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin and Security administrator as role groups for creating and deploying policies.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator

claims.claim: NotifyPolicyTipUrl is documented for the popup URL in Exchange workloads.
claims.quote: The NotifyPolicyTipUrl parameter specifies the URL in the popup dialog for Exchange workloads. This URL value has priority over the global: Set-PolicyConfig -ComplianceUrl.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant-wide switch specifically for notification hyperlinks.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP hyperlink tenant; Endpoint DLP Edge notification hyperlink Get Support default existing notifications tenant switch PowerShell. Read endpoint settings and DLP policy reference; no hyperlink-specific tenant switch documented.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP notifications on Windows 10/11 are associated with sensitive activity matching a rule.
claims.quote: When a user attempts an activity on a sensitive item in a context that meets the conditions of a rule ... you can let them know about it ... plus the option to customize the notification title, content, and add a hyperlink ... that appears on the Windows 10/11 device.

claims.claim: Adding notification hyperlinks makes no change to what DLP detects.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP hyperlink notification changes detection blocking actions existing rules rollout. Read roadmap 558688, DLP policy reference and Edge DLP page; they describe notification customisation, not an explicit unchanged-detection guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change to what DLP detects or blocks.' with 'The roadmap describes this change as adding hyperlinks to Edge warn and block notifications.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The hyperlink does not change the rule's auditing, warning or blocking behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP hyperlink notification changes detection blocking actions existing rules rollout. Opened DLP policy reference, deployment guide and Edge DLP page; rule actions are documented but no hyperlink-specific unchanged-enforcement statement found.
claims.fix: Remove 'The hyperlink does not change that.' Replace the risk rationale with: 'Low. The roadmap describes a link in an Edge warn or block notification. Microsoft has not stated what happens to existing notifications on arrival.' Apply the replacement of 'No change to what DLP detects or blocks.' specified for the detection claim.

claims.claim: Only rules an administrator gives a hyperlink show one.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP hyperlink default Edge; Endpoint DLP hyperlinks notification only; notification changes existing rules rollout. Read roadmap 558688, DLP policy reference and endpoint settings; no statement excludes automatic or pre-existing links on arrival.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: 'Low. The roadmap describes hyperlinks in notifications shown when an Edge rule triggers; Microsoft has not stated what happens to existing notifications on arrival.' The 'Expect' sentence in Why it matters is analysis, not evidence for this categorical default claim.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to check Activity explorer, but the controls table has no monitoring row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check Activity explorer for blocked and overridden events'. Table rows: 'Whether Edge activities ... are audited, warned ... or blocked' and 'Custom notification title, content and hyperlink'. Neither gives Activity explorer.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Check Activity explorer for blocked and overridden events from the rules that carry a link, to see whether overrides change.' Do not add a control row during this correction.
